detours.why: D-666 ARM B: this B.Cu segment TERMINATES at the barrel (59.300,106.300) the same spec removes.  Relaying it between its own two ends asks the router to reach a site that is reserved and a bond that is gone; ARM A asked exactly that and got NO_PATH at 0.300 mm inside a 5.180 mm budget.  It is a stub of a removed bond, so it is REMOVED AND NOT PUT BACK and the gate's inert_removal_priced clause prices it.

note: D-666 ARM E -- the promotable shape.  Same EIGHT units as arms A-D, the STATED LANE of arm D (evidence/d666-wake-lane-guard.json) as --guard, and each relay STATES ITS OWN max_mm.  Arm D refused because emptying the per-site reserve discs collapsed the default relay budget to `was + 2*pi*R_max + movemm` with R_max = 0 -- that is the removed length EXACTLY, 5.136 mm for /IR_TX_GPIO16 and 2.4 mm for /SX1262_CS_N, so neither relay was allowed a single millimetre to go around anything.  The default bound is written for a detour past DISCS; a detour past a LANE is a longer walk and the spec has to own that judgement out loud (route_maze_batch.py: 'a spec may state its own max_mm and own that judgement explicitly').  15.0 mm and 12.0 mm, about 3x and 5x the copper removed: /IR_TX_GPIO16 is the IR transmit drive at a 38 kHz carrier and /SX1262_CS_N is a LoRa chip select -- neither is a length-critical net, and both stay far inside the DRU's 25 mm uncoupled budget.
